32: /graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
33: /graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)

37: /graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it

46: ## What graphify is for
47: 
48: Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

50: **When a graph is worth building:** this applies when you are choosing a tool yourself; if the user invoked `/graphify`, follow that request as asked. AST extraction of code is fast and free, but semantic extraction of docs, papers and images runs the model over every file, which can cost minutes and tens of thousands of tokens.

52: If a graph already exists, query it. With no graph, one targeted lookup ("where is X defined", "what calls Y" in an ordinary-sized codebase) is faster and free with a plain text search such as `grep` and `Read`: search directly instead of running the steps below, and mention that a graph can be built if the user wants one. Build one when you expect many questions against this corpus, the corpus is large or unfamiliar, the question needs links text search cannot see (doc to code, across documents), or it is structural (communities, bridges, import cycles).

54: ## What You Must Do When Invoked
55: 
56: If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

58: **Fast path — existing graph:** Before doing anything else, check whether `graphify-out/graph.json` exists. The expected location is `graphify-out/graph.json` relative to the **current working directory** (i.e. the project root where you are running commands). If it exists AND the user's request is a natural-language question about the codebase (e.g. "How does X work?", "What calls Y?", "Trace the data flow through Z") and NOT an explicit rebuild command (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, or a bare path/URL that implies fresh extraction): **skip Steps 1–5 entirely and jump straight to `## For /graphify query`.** Run `graphify query "<question>"` immediately. 66: ### Step 0 - GitHub repos and multi-path merge (only if a URL or several paths)

74: PYTHON=""
75: GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)

90: if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then PYTHON="python3"; fi

102: mkdir -p graphify-out

105: # The scan path is passed through a quoted heredoc, never substituted into the
106: # command line itself: a bare `cd <path>` (or an unquoted heredoc, which
107: # still expands $()/backticks in its body) would let a malicious path execute
108: # as shell code the moment this line runs.

119:

122: import json
123: from graphify.detect import detect
124: from pathlib import Path
125: from graphify.paths import out_path
126: from graphify.watch import _read_build_excludes, _read_build_gitignore
127: result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'), extra_excludes=_read_build_excludes(out_path()), gitignore=_read_build_gitignore(out_path()))

129: # on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528).

166: **Before starting:** note whether `--mode deep` was given. You must pass `DEEP_MODE=true` to every subagent in Step B2 if it was. Track this from the original invocation - do not lose it.

168: This step has two parts: **structural extraction** (deterministic, free) and **semantic extraction** (LLM, costs tokens).
169: 
170: > **graphify needs no API key. Never ask the user for one, and never block on one.** Code is extracted structurally (AST) with no LLM and no key at all — a code-only corpus (the common `/graphify .` on a repo) skips semantic extraction entirely, so it needs nothing here: go straight to Part A and skip Part B. Semantic extraction (only for docs, papers, and images) uses Gemini **only if** `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` is already set; otherwise the host agent itself is the LLM. graphify does **not** read `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or any other provider key. If you catch yourself about to prompt for, wait on, or stop because of a missing API key, that is a misread of this skill — proceed without one.
171: 
172: **Before semantic extraction:** check whether `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is set. If neither is set, print this one-liner to the user:
173: > Tip: set `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` to use Gemini for semantic extraction (`pip install 'graphifyy[gemini]'`).
174: 
175: Print it once, then continue — do not wait for the user to supply a key. If `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` IS set, use `graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(files, backend="gemini")` for semantic extraction instead of dispatching subagents. The default Gemini model is `gemini-3-flash-preview`; set `GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL` or pass `--model` in headless CLI flows to override it.
176: 
177: > **No other API keys are read.** When `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY` are unset, semantic extraction falls to the host agent itself — the running session is the LLM. On a host that dispatches subagents (e.g. Claude Code), dispatch them as written in Part B. On a host that runs the CLI directly in a terminal and cannot dispatch subagents, do not stall: a code-only corpus has no semantic work, so write the empty semantic file (Part B "Fast path") and continue to Part C; for a corpus with docs/papers/images, either set a Gemini key or extract those inline yourself, but in no case prompt for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — that prompt is a misread of this skill.
178: 
179: **Run Part A (AST) and Part B (semantic) in parallel. Dispatch all semantic subagents AND start AST extraction in the same message. Both can run simultaneously since they operate on different file types. Merge results in Part C as before.**
180: 
181: Note: Parallelizing AST + semantic saves 5-15s on large corpora. AST is deterministic and fast; start it while subagents are processing docs/papers.
182: 
183: #### Part A - Structural extraction for code files
184: 
185: For any code files detected, run AST extraction in parallel with Part B subagents:
186: 
187: ```bash
188: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
189: import sys, json
190: from graphify.extract import collect_files, extract
191: from pathlib import Path
192: import json
193: 
194: code_files = []
195: detect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
196: for f in detect.get('files', {}).get('code', []):
197:     code_files.extend(collect_files(Path(f)) if Path(f).is_dir() else [Path(f)])
198: 
199: if code_files:
200:     # root= anchors node ids and source_file on the scan root; cache_root only says
201:     # where graphify-out/cache lives. Pass both: without root= the anchor falls back
202:     # to cache_root, so pointing the cache elsewhere would rename every node (#3727).
203:     result = extract(code_files, cache_root=Path('INPUT_PATH'), root=Path('INPUT_PATH'))
204:     Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
205:     print(f'AST: {len(result[\"nodes\"])} nodes, {len(result[\"edges\"])} edges')
206: else:
207:     Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes':[],'edges':[],'input_tokens':0,'output_tokens':0}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
208:     print('No code files - skipping AST extraction')
209: "
210: ```
211: 
212: #### Part B - Semantic extraction (parallel subagents)
213: 
214: **Fast path:** If detection found zero docs, papers, and images (code-only corpus), skip Part B entirely and go straight to Part C. AST handles code - there is nothing for semantic subagents to do. **First write an empty semantic file** so Part C's merge has its input (it reads `.graphify_semantic.json` unconditionally; without this a code-only run hits `FileNotFoundError`):
215: 
216: ```bash
217: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
218: import json
219: from pathlib import Path
220: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[],'input_tokens':0,'output_tokens':0}), encoding='utf-8')
221: "
222: ```
223: 
224: **MANDATORY: You MUST use the Agent tool here. Reading files yourself one-by-one is forbidden - it is 5-10x slower. If you do not use the Agent tool you are doing this wrong.**
225: 
226: Before dispatching subagents, print a timing estimate:
227: - Load `total_words` and file counts from `graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json`
228: - Estimate agents needed: `ceil(uncached_non_code_files / 22)` (chunk size is 20-25 files, capped at ~6000 total lines)
229: - Estimate time: ~45s per agent batch (they run in parallel, so total ≈ 45s × ceil(agents/parallel_limit))
230: - Print: "Semantic extraction: ~N files → X agents, estimated ~Ys"
231: 
232: **Step B0 - Check extraction cache first**
233: 
234: Before dispatching any subagents, check which files already have cached extraction results:
235: 
236: SPEC_PATH below is the **absolute** path of the `references/extraction-spec.md` that ships beside this SKILL.md — the same file Step B2 loads and hands to every subagent. It is the extraction prompt, so cache entries are attributed to it: when a graphify upgrade changes the prompt, entries produced by the old one are re-extracted instead of replayed, and unchanged prompts keep their entries (#1939). Substitute the real path in both Step B0 and Step B3 — pass the same one to each, and do not drop the argument.
237: 
238: ```bash
239: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
240: import json
241: from graphify.cache import check_semantic_cache
242: from pathlib import Path
243: 
244: detect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
245: # Only content files go to semantic extraction. Code is already covered structurally
246: # by the AST pass (Part A); flattening every category here makes subagents re-read
247: # every source file (#1392). Video is transcribed to a document in Step 2.5 first.
248: all_files = [f for cat in ('document', 'paper', 'image') for f in detect['files'].get(cat, [])]
249: 
250: cached_nodes, cached_edges, cached_hyperedges, uncached = check_semantic_cache(all_files, root='INPUT_PATH', prompt_file='SPEC_PATH')
251: 
252: # Always (re)write the cache file: write hits, else DELETE any leftover from a prior
253: # run so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json (#1392).
254: if cached_nodes or cached_edges or cached_hyperedges:
255:     Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes': cached_nodes, 'edges': cached_edges, 'hyperedges': cached_hyperedges}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
256: else:
257:     Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').unlink(missing_ok=True)
258: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').write_text('\n'.join(uncached), encoding=\"utf-8\")
259: # Nothing has been dispatched yet, so any chunk file on disk is a leftover from an
260: # interrupted run, and Step B3 merges every .graphify_chunk_*.json it finds.
261: for stale in Path('graphify-out').glob('.graphify_chunk_*.json'):
262:     stale.unlink()
263: print(f'Cache: {len(all_files)-len(uncached)} files hit, {len(uncached)} files need extraction')
264: "
265: ```
266: 
267: Only dispatch subagents for files listed in `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. If all files are cached, skip Steps B1 and B2 but still run Step B3's commands: its merge is the only Part B step that writes `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json`, and Part C reads that file unconditionally. Do not write an empty `.graphify_semantic.json` instead, because that drops every cached node.
268: 
269: **Step B1 - Split into chunks**
270: 
271: Load files from `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. Split into chunks bounded by BOTH limits: at most 20-25 files AND at most ~6000 total lines per chunk. A text file longer than 2000 lines gets a chunk to itself - that is past the Read tool's single-call cap, so sharing a chunk with other files guarantees it is only partly read. Each image gets its own chunk (vision needs separate context). When splitting, group files from the same directory together so related artifacts land in the same chunk and cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.
272: 
273: Both bounds matter. The line bound is not only about the 2000-line Read cap: a subagent holding 25 files splits its attention across all of them and skims the dense ones, and a 590-line plan can come back with zero nodes that way. Bounding content as well as file count is what keeps a chunk's coverage honest (#2225).
274: 
275: **Step B2 - Dispatch ALL subagents in a single message**
276: 
277: > Uses the `Task` tool for parallel subagent dispatch.
278: > Call `Task` once per chunk — ALL in the same response so they run in parallel.
279: 
280: Pass the extraction prompt as the task description:
281: 
282: ```
283: Task(description="Your task is to perform the following. Follow the instructions below exactly.\n\n<agent-instructions>\n[extraction prompt, with FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE substituted]\n</agent-instructions>\n\nExecute this now. Output ONLY the structured JSON response.")
284: ```

286: Each subagent writes its result to its own `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json`. Collect results as each `Task` completes and parse each as JSON.

288: CHUNK_PATH must be an **absolute** path — derive it before dispatching:
289: ```bash
290: PROJECT_ROOT=$(pwd)  # cwd — where Part C globs graphify-out/ (NOT .graphify_root/scan dir, #1392)
291: # Then for chunk N: CHUNK_PATH="${PROJECT_ROOT}/graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_0N.json"

1: # graphify reference: extraction subagent prompt
2: 
3: Load this in Step 3 Part B when the corpus has at least one doc, paper, or image chunk. A pure-code corpus skips Part B and never reads this file. Each semantic subagent receives the prompt below verbatim (substitute FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH).
4: 
5: ```
6: You are a graphify extraction subagent. Read the files listed and extract a knowledge graph fragment.
7: Output ONLY valid JSON matching the schema below - no explanation, no markdown fences, no preamble.
8: 
9: Files (chunk CHUNK_NUM of TOTAL_CHUNKS):
10: FILE_LIST
11: 
12: Read every file in this list COMPLETELY before extracting anything from it. The Read tool
13: returns at most 2000 lines per call and reports NO error and NO warning when it truncates, so a
14: long file silently yields a partial extraction. When a file is longer than one call, keep paging
15: with offset/limit until you have actually seen its last line - never assume the first call
16: returned the whole file. Never emit nodes for a file you have only partly read. A partial
17: extraction is worse than none: replace-on-re-extract first DROPS that file's existing nodes and
18: then re-adds only what you saw, so the unread tail disappears from the graph, and the file is then
19: recorded as successfully extracted and never retried (#2225).
20: 
21: Report the coverage you actually achieved, so a short read is caught instead of guessed at: add a
22: top-level "coverage" object mapping each FILE_LIST path you extracted to the number of lines you
23: read, e.g. {"coverage": {"docs/plan.md": 452}}. If you could not reach a file's last line, still
24: report the count you did read. A short count is recoverable - Step B3 warns, the entry is cached
25: as partial, and the next --update retries the file - whereas a missing entry is indistinguishable
26: from a complete read.
27: 
28: Rules:
29: - EXTRACTED: relationship explicit in source (import, call, citation, "see §3.2")
30: - INFERRED: reasonable inference (shared data structure, implied dependency)
31: - AMBIGUOUS: uncertain - flag for review, do not omit
32: 
33: Code files: focus on semantic edges AST cannot find (call relationships, shared data, arch patterns).
34:   Do not re-extract imports - AST already has those.
35: Doc/paper files: extract named concepts, entities, citations. For rationale (WHY decisions were made, trade-offs, design intent): store as a `rationale` attribute on the relevant concept node — do NOT create a separate rationale node or fragment node. Only create a node for something that is itself a named entity or concept. Use `file_type:"rationale"` for concept-like nodes (ideas, principles, mechanisms, design patterns). `file_type` MUST be one of exactly these six values: `code`, `document`, `paper`, `image`, `rationale`, `concept`. Any other value is invalid and will be rejected.
36: Code files: when adding `calls` edges, source MUST be the caller (the function/class doing the calling), target MUST be the callee. Never reverse this direction. `calls` edges MUST stay within one language: a Python function cannot `calls` a JS/TS/Go/Rust/Java symbol and vice versa — cross-language call edges are phantom artifacts, never emit them.
37: Image files: use vision to understand what the image IS - do not just OCR.
38:   UI screenshot: layout patterns, design decisions, key elements, purpose.
39:   Chart: metric, trend/insight, data source.
40:   Tweet/post: claim as node, author, concepts mentioned.
41:   Diagram: components and connections.
42:   Research figure: what it demonstrates, method, result.
43:   Handwritten/whiteboard: ideas and arrows, mark uncertain readings AMBIGUOUS.
44: 
45: DEEP_MODE (if --mode deep was given): be aggressive with INFERRED edges - indirect deps,
46:   shared assumptions, latent couplings. Mark uncertain ones AMBIGUOUS instead of omitting.
47: 
48: Semantic similarity: if two concepts in this chunk solve the same problem or represent the same idea without any structural link (no import, no call, no citation), add a `semantically_similar_to` edge marked INFERRED with a confidence_score reflecting how similar they are (0.6-0.95). Examples:
49: - Two functions that both validate user input but never call each other
50: - A class in code and a concept in a paper that describe the same algorithm
51: - Two error types that handle the same failure mode differently
52: Only add these when the similarity is genuinely non-obvious and cross-cutting. Do not add them for trivially similar things.
53: 
54: Hyperedges: if 3 or more nodes clearly participate together in a shared concept, flow, or pattern that is not captured by pairwise edges alone, add a hyperedge to a top-level `hyperedges` array. Examples:
55: - All classes that implement a common protocol or interface
56: - All functions in an authentication flow (even if they don't all call each other)
57: - All concepts from a paper section that form one coherent idea
58: Use sparingly — only when the group relationship adds information beyond the pairwise edges. Maximum 3 hyperedges per chunk.
59: 
60: If a file has YAML frontmatter (--- ... ---), copy source_url, captured_at, author,
61:   contributor onto every node from that file.
62: 
63: confidence_score is REQUIRED on every edge - never omit it, never use 0.5 as a default:
64: - EXTRACTED edges: confidence_score = 1.0 always
65: - INFERRED edges: pick exactly ONE value from this set — never 0.5:
66:     0.95  direct structural evidence (shared data structure, named cross-file reference).
67:     0.85  strong inference (clear functional alignment, no direct symbol link).
68:     0.75  reasonable inference (shared problem domain + similar shape, requires interpretation).
69:     0.65  weak inference (thematically related, no shape evidence).
70:     0.55  speculative but plausible (surface-level co-occurrence only).
71:   Models follow discrete rubrics better than continuous ranges; the bimodal
72:   distribution observed in production (>50% at 0.5, >40% at 0.85+) shows the
73:   range guidance is being collapsed to a binary. If no value above fits, mark
74:   the edge AMBIGUOUS rather than picking 0.4 or below.
75: - AMBIGUOUS edges: 0.1-0.3
76: 
77: Node ID format: lowercase, word characters only (`[^\W]` after casefolding — `[a-z0-9_]` for ASCII input, but non-ASCII letters and digits are kept as-is), no dots or slashes. Format: `{stem}_{entity}` where stem is the **full repo-relative path with the extension dropped**, every path segment kept and joined with `_` (each segment lowercased with non-alphanumeric chars replaced by `_`), and entity is the symbol name similarly normalized. Use every directory level, not just the immediate parent — this keeps same-named files in different directories distinct. Examples: `src/auth/session.py` + `ValidateToken` → `src_auth_session_validatetoken`; `lib/utils/helpers.py` + `parse_url` → `lib_utils_helpers_parse_url`; `tests/test_foo.py` + `_helper` → `tests_test_foo_helper`; `docs/v1/api/README.md` + `getUser` → `docs_v1_api_readme_getuser`. Top-level files (no parent dir, e.g. `setup.py`) use just the filename stem: `setup_my_func`. This must match the ID the AST extractor generates — using just the filename (e.g., `session_validatetoken`) or only the immediate parent (e.g., `auth_session_validatetoken`) will create orphan ghost-duplicate nodes. If you are re-extracting a project built under the old immediate-parent format, the user should run `graphify extract --force` to rebuild cleanly. CRITICAL: never append chunk numbers, sequence numbers, or any suffix to an ID (no `_c1`, `_c2`, `_chunk2`, etc.). IDs must be deterministic from the label alone — the same entity must always produce the same ID regardless of which chunk processes it.
78: 
79: Generate the extraction JSON matching this schema exactly:
80: {"nodes":[{"id":"auth_session_validatetoken","label":"Human Readable Name","file_type":"code|document|paper|image|rationale|concept","source_file":"<FILE_LIST path verbatim>","source_location":null,"source_url":null,"captured_at":null,"author":null,"contributor":null}],"edges":[{"source":"node_id","target":"node_id","relation":"calls|implements|references|cites|conceptually_related_to|shares_data_with|semantically_similar_to|rationale_for","confidence":"EXTRACTED|INFERRED|AMBIGUOUS","confidence_score":1.0,"source_file":"<FILE_LIST path verbatim>","source_location":null,"weight":1.0}],"hyperedges":[{"id":"snake_case_id","label":"Human Readable Label","nodes":["node_id1","node_id2","node_id3"],"relation":"participate_in|implement|form","confidence":"EXTRACTED|INFERRED","confidence_score":0.75,"source_file":"<FILE_LIST path verbatim>"}],"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"coverage":{"<FILE_LIST path verbatim>":0}}
81: 
82: source_file RULE (every node, edge, and hyperedge): set source_file to the path of the originating file EXACTLY as it appears in FILE_LIST — verbatim and absolute. Do NOT shorten to a basename, do NOT re-relativize, do NOT strip any directory prefix, and do NOT change separators (the engine canonicalizes separators and relativizes against the build root downstream). Copy the FILE_LIST entry character-for-character. This keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base, so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.
83: 
84: Then write the JSON to disk using the Write tool at this exact absolute path (no relative paths — Write resolves relative paths against an undefined cwd and the file will be silently lost):
85: CHUNK_PATH
86: ```

248: all_files = [f for cat in ('document', 'paper', 'image') for f in detect['files'].get(cat, [])]
249: 
250: cached_nodes, cached_edges, cached_hyperedges, uncached = check_semantic_cache(all_files, root='INPUT_PATH', prompt_file='SPEC_PATH')
251: 
252: # Always (re)write the cache file: write hits, else DELETE any leftover from a prior
253: # run so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json (#1392).
254: if cached_nodes or cached_edges or cached_hyperedges:
255:     Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').write_text(json.dumps({'nodes': cached_nodes, 'edges': cached_edges, 'hyperedges': cached_hyperedges}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
256: else:
257:     Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').unlink(missing_ok=True)
258: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').write_text('\n'.join(uncached), encoding=\"utf-8\")
259: # Nothing has been dispatched yet, so any chunk file on disk is a leftover from an
260: # interrupted run, and Step B3 merges every .graphify_chunk_*.json it finds.
261: for stale in Path('graphify-out').glob('.graphify_chunk_*.json'):
262:     stale.unlink()
263: print(f'Cache: {len(all_files)-len(uncached)} files hit, {len(uncached)} files need extraction')
264: "
265: ```
266: 
267: Only dispatch subagents for files listed in `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. If all files are cached, skip Steps B1 and B2 but still run Step B3's commands: its merge is the only Part B step that writes `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json`, and Part C reads that file unconditionally. Do not write an empty `.graphify_semantic.json` instead, because that drops every cached node.
268: 
269: **Step B1 - Split into chunks**
270: 
271: Load files from `graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt`. Split into chunks bounded by BOTH limits: at most 20-25 files AND at most ~6000 total lines per chunk. A text file longer than 2000 lines gets a chunk to itself - that is past the Read tool's single-call cap, so sharing a chunk with other files guarantees it is only partly read. Each image gets its own chunk (vision needs separate context). When splitting, group files from the same directory together so related artifacts land in the same chunk and cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.
272: 
273: Both bounds matter. The line bound is not only about the 2000-line Read cap: a subagent holding 25 files splits its attention across all of them and skims the dense ones, and a 590-line plan can come back with zero nodes that way. Bounding content as well as file count is what keeps a chunk's coverage honest (#2225).
274: 
275: **Step B2 - Dispatch ALL subagents in a single message**
276: 
277: > Uses the `Task` tool for parallel subagent dispatch.
278: > Call `Task` once per chunk — ALL in the same response so they run in parallel.
279: 
280: Pass the extraction prompt as the task description:
281: 
282: ```
283: Task(description="Your task is to perform the following. Follow the instructions below exactly.\n\n<agent-instructions>\n[extraction prompt, with FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE substituted]\n</agent-instructions>\n\nExecute this now. Output ONLY the structured JSON response.")
284: ```
285: 
286: Each subagent writes its result to its own `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json`. Collect results as each `Task` completes and parse each as JSON.
287: 
288: CHUNK_PATH must be an **absolute** path — derive it before dispatching:
289: ```bash
290: PROJECT_ROOT=$(pwd)  # cwd — where Part C globs graphify-out/ (NOT .graphify_root/scan dir, #1392)
291: # Then for chunk N: CHUNK_PATH="${PROJECT_ROOT}/graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_0N.json"
292: ```
293: 
294: Subagent prompt template:
295: 
296: See `references/extraction-spec.md` for the exact subagent prompt (JSON schema, node-ID rules, confidence rubric, hyperedge, and vision rules). Load it only here, only when at least one chunk holds a doc, paper, or image; a pure-code corpus has skipped Part B and never reads it. Pass each subagent that prompt verbatim with FILE_LIST, CHUNK_NUM, TOTAL_CHUNKS, DEEP_MODE, and CHUNK_PATH substituted, and have it write the result to CHUNK_PATH.
297: 
298: **Step B3 - Collect, cache, and merge**
299: 
300: Wait for all subagents. For each result:
301: - Check that `graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_NN.json` exists on disk — this is the success signal
302: - If the file exists and contains valid JSON with `nodes` and `edges`, include it and save to cache
303: - If the file is missing, the subagent was likely dispatched as read-only (Explore type) — print a warning: "chunk N missing from disk — subagent may have been read-only. Re-run with general-purpose agent." Do not silently skip.
304: - If a subagent failed or returned invalid JSON, print a warning and skip that chunk - do not abort
305: 
306: If more than half the chunks failed or are missing, stop and tell the user to re-run and ensure `subagent_type="general-purpose"` is used.
307: 
308: **Step B3.5 - Verify each reported file was actually read to its end**
309: 
310: A subagent that only read the first Read call's worth of a long file still writes a well-formed chunk, so "chunk file exists and parses" is not evidence of coverage. Compare each file's self-reported `coverage` against its real length:
311: 
312: ```bash
313: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
314: import json, glob
315: from pathlib import Path
316: 
317: covered = {}
318: for c in sorted(glob.glob('graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json')):
319:     d = json.loads(Path(c).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
320:     for src, n in (d.get('coverage') or {}).items():
321:         covered[src] = max(covered.get(src, 0), int(n))
322: 
323: partial = []
324: for src, n in sorted(covered.items()):
325:     p = Path(src)
326:     if not p.is_absolute():
327:         p = Path('INPUT_PATH') / src
328:     if not p.is_file():
329:         continue
330:     total = sum(1 for _ in p.open(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
331:     if total and n < total:
332:         partial.append((src, n, total))
333: 
334: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').write_text('\n'.join(s for s, _, _ in partial), encoding=\"utf-8\")
335: if partial:
336:     print(f'WARNING: {len(partial)} file(s) were only partly read. They are cached as partial and retried on the next --update:')
337:     for src, n, total in partial:
338:         print(f'  {src}: read {n} of {total} lines')
339: else:
340:     print('Coverage OK - every file a subagent reported was read to its last line')
341: "
342: ```
343: 
344: Tell the user which files came up short and what was lost (the line counts are printed above). The nodes already extracted for those files are kept - they are still true - but the file is cached as partial and left unstamped in the manifest below, so the next `--update` re-dispatches it and replace-on-re-extract swaps the partial node set for a complete one. This is the same mechanism the library path uses for a truncated LLM response (#933, #1950), so both paths now recover instead of silently keeping a half-read file forever. A file a subagent did not report at all is not counted as partial - there is nothing to compare against - which is why the prompt rule in `references/extraction-spec.md` asks for the count in the first place.
345: 
346: Merge all chunk files into `.graphify_semantic_new.json`. **After each Agent call completes, read the real token counts from the Agent tool result's `usage` field and write them back into the chunk JSON before merging** — the chunk JSON itself always has placeholder zeros. Then run:
347: ```bash
348: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
349: import json, glob
350: from pathlib import Path
351: 
352: chunks = sorted(glob.glob('graphify-out/.graphify_chunk_*.json'))
353: all_nodes, all_edges, all_hyperedges = [], [], []
354: total_in, total_out = 0, 0
355: for c in chunks:
356:     d = json.loads(Path(c).read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
357:     all_nodes += d.get('nodes', [])
358:     all_edges += d.get('edges', [])
359:     all_hyperedges += d.get('hyperedges', [])
360:     total_in += d.get('input_tokens', 0)
361:     total_out += d.get('output_tokens', 0)
362: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').write_text(json.dumps({
363:     'nodes': all_nodes, 'edges': all_edges, 'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,
364:     'input_tokens': total_in, 'output_tokens': total_out,
365: }, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
366: print(f'Merged {len(chunks)} chunks: {total_in:,} in / {total_out:,} out tokens')
367: "
368: ```
369: 
370: Save new results to cache. Pass the same SPEC_PATH as Step B0 — it stamps each entry with the prompt that produced it, and a write under a different prompt than the read lands where the next run won't look (#1939):
371: ```bash
372: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
373: import json
374: from graphify.cache import save_semantic_cache
375: from pathlib import Path
376: 
377: new = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}
378: uncached = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_uncached.txt').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines() if line]
379: # A partly-read file is cached with partial: True, which load_cached treats as a MISS,
380: # so the next --update re-dispatches it instead of serving a truncated extraction forever
381: # (#2225). Same contract the library path uses for a truncated LLM response (#933/#1950).
382: partial = [line for line in Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines() if line] if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt').exists() else []
383: saved = save_semantic_cache(new.get('nodes', []), new.get('edges', []), new.get('hyperedges', []), root='INPUT_PATH', allowed_source_files=uncached, prompt_file='SPEC_PATH', partial_source_files=partial)
384: note = f' ({len(partial)} left partial for retry)' if partial else ''
385: print(f'Cached {saved} files' + note)
386: "
387: ```
388: 
389: Merge cached + new results into `graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json`:
390: ```bash
391: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
392: import json
393: from pathlib import Path
394: 
395: cached = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_cached.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}
396: new = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) if Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic_new.json').exists() else {'nodes':[],'edges':[],'hyperedges':[]}
397: 
398: all_nodes = cached['nodes'] + new.get('nodes', [])
399: all_edges = cached['edges'] + new.get('edges', [])
400: all_hyperedges = cached.get('hyperedges', []) + new.get('hyperedges', [])
401: seen = set()
402: deduped = []
403: for n in all_nodes:
404:     if n['id'] not in seen:
405:         seen.add(n['id'])
406:         deduped.append(n)
407: 
408: merged = {
409:     'nodes': deduped,
410:     'edges': all_edges,
411:     'hyperedges': all_hyperedges,
412:     'input_tokens': new.get('input_tokens', 0),
413:     'output_tokens': new.get('output_tokens', 0),
414: }
415: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
416: print(f'Extraction complete - {len(deduped)} nodes, {len(all_edges)} edges ({len(cached[\"nodes\"])} from cache, {len(new.get(\"nodes\",[]))} new)')
417: "
418: ```

421: #### Part C - Merge AST + semantic into final extraction
422: 
423: ```bash
424: $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
425: import sys, json
426: from pathlib import Path
427: 
428: ast = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
429: sem = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json').read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
430: 
431: # Stamp tier provenance on the semantic side. build._is_ast_tier reads
432: # _origin when present and otherwise guesses from the SHAPE of
433: # source_location ('L<line>' means AST). A subagent that writes 'L12' for a
434: # doc section therefore made that node read as AST, and the next
435: # graphify update deleted it along with the re-extracted code file it
436: # seemed to belong to (#2843). extract() stamps its own items 'ast'; the
437: # semantic side must say so explicitly.
438: for n in sem['nodes']:
439:     n.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')
440: for e in sem['edges']:
441:     e.setdefault('_origin', 'semantic')
442: 
443: # Merge: AST nodes first, semantic nodes deduplicated by id
444: seen = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}
445: merged_nodes = list(ast['nodes'])
446: for n in sem['nodes']:
447:     if n['id'] not in seen:
448:         merged_nodes.append(n)
449:         seen.add(n['id'])
450: 
451: merged_edges = ast['edges'] + sem['edges']
452: merged_hyperedges = sem.get('hyperedges', [])
453: merged = {
454:     'nodes': merged_nodes,
455:     'edges': merged_edges,
456:     'hyperedges': merged_hyperedges,
457:     'input_tokens': sem.get('input_tokens', 0),
458:     'output_tokens': sem.get('output_tokens', 0),
459: }
460: Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').write_text(json.dumps(merged, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
461: total = len(merged_nodes)
462: edges = len(merged_edges)
463: print(f'Merged: {total} nodes, {edges} edges ({len(ast[\"nodes\"])} AST + {len(sem[\"nodes\"])} semantic)')
464: "
465: ```

Replace `IS_FORCE` with `True` if `--force` was given (permits intentional shrink, e.g. after deleting files), otherwise `False`. 650: # a detected file whose chunk failed or was omitted must stay unstamped so the
651: # next --update re-queues it, otherwise it is marked done and its content is lost
652: # forever (#2015). This mirrors the library extract path exactly
653: # (cli._stamped_manifest_files + clear_semantic + scan_corpus); do not stamp the
654: # raw corpus. Code files are always stamped (AST is deterministic); only semantic
655: # types are gated on output.
656: from graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files
657: _corpus = detect.get('all_files') or detect['files']
658: # A file a subagent only partly read DID produce output, so the stamp filter alone would
659: # keep it - but its node set covers just the head of the file, and stamping it means
660: # detect_incremental reads it as done and never re-queues it, leaving the truncated graph
661: # live forever. Name those files so they stay unstamped and are retried next run (#2225).
662: _pf = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt')
663: _partial = {l.strip() for l in _pf.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines() if l.strip()} if _pf.exists() else set()
664: _manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path('INPUT_PATH'), partial_source_files=_partial)
665: # Files dispatched this run (the changed subset) but NOT stamped above still carry
666: # a stale semantic_hash from a prior run; clear it so detect_incremental re-queues
667: # them instead of reading them as unchanged (#1948).
668: _sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')
669: _dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}
670: _stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}
671: _cleared = _dispatched - _stamped
672: # scan_corpus = the RAW full corpus (not the stamp-filtered subset) so in-root
673: # files newly excluded since last run are dropped rather than masquerading as
674: # deletions; untouched files' prior rows are still preserved (#1908).
675: _scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}
676: save_manifest(_manifest_files, root='INPUT_PATH', scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)
677: 
678: # Update cumulative cost tracker
679: input_tok = extract.get('input_tokens', 0)
680: output_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)
681: 
682: cost_path = Path('graphify-out/cost.json')
683: if cost_path.exists():
684:     cost = json.loads(cost_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))
685: else:
686:     cost = {'runs': [], 'total_input_tokens': 0, 'total_output_tokens': 0}
687: 
688: cost['runs'].append({
689:     'date': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
690:     'input_tokens': input_tok,
691:     'output_tokens': output_tok,
692:     'files': detect.get('total_files', 0),
693: })
694: cost['total_input_tokens'] += input_tok
695: cost['total_output_tokens'] += output_tok
696: cost_path.write_text(json.dumps(cost, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")
697: 
698: print(f'This run: {input_tok:,} input tokens, {output_tok:,} output tokens')
699: print(f'All time: {cost[\"total_input_tokens\"]:,} input, {cost[\"total_output_tokens\"]:,} output ({len(cost[\"runs\"])} runs)')
700: "
701: rm -f graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json graphify-out/.graphify_ast.json graphify-out/.graphify_semantic.json graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt
702: find graphify-out -maxdepth 1 -name '.graphify_chunk_*.json' -delete 2>/dev/null
703: rm -f graphify-out/.needs_update 2>/dev/null || true
704: ```
705: 
706: Replace INPUT_PATH with the actual path (same value used in Steps 4-5) so the manifest is relativized to the scan root.
707: 
708: Tell the user (omit the obsidian line unless --obsidian was given):
709: ```
710: Graph complete. Outputs in PATH_TO_DIR/graphify-out/
711: 
712:   graph.html            - interactive graph, open in browser
713:   GRAPH_REPORT.md       - audit report
714:   graph.json            - raw graph data
715:   obsidian/             - Obsidian vault (only if --obsidian was given)
716: ```
717: 
718: If graphify saved you time, consider supporting it: https://github.com/sponsors/safishamsi
719: 
720: Replace PATH_TO_DIR with the actual absolute path of the directory that was processed.
721: 
722: If PATH_TO_DIR is inside a git repository, add one line to the report: `graphify-out/` was written into the working tree, so unless the repository already ignores it, it will show in `git status`; the user can add `graphify-out/` to `.gitignore`, or commit only the outputs their team should share (see https://docs.graphify.com/guides/team-workflows).
723: 
724: Then paste these sections from GRAPH_REPORT.md directly into the chat:
725: - God Nodes
726: - Surprising Connections
727: - Suggested Questions
728: 
729: Do NOT paste the full report - just those three sections. Keep it concise.
730: 
731: Then immediately offer to explore. Pick the single most interesting suggested question from the report - the one that crosses the most community boundaries or has the most surprising bridge node - and ask:
732: 
733: > "The most interesting question this graph can answer: **[question]**. Want me to trace it?"
734: 
735: If the user says yes, run `/graphify query "[question]"` on the graph and walk them through the answer using the graph structure - which nodes connect, which community boundaries get crossed, what the path reveals. Keep going as long as they want to explore. Each answer should end with a natural follow-up ("this connects to X - want to go deeper?") so the session feels like navigation, not a one-shot report.
736: 
737: The graph is the map. Your job after the pipeline is to be the guide.
738: 
739: ---
740: 
741: ## Interpreter guard for subcommands
742: 
743: Before running any subcommand below (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, `query`, `path`, `explain`, `add`), check that `.graphify_python` exists. If it's missing (e.g. user deleted `graphify-out/`), re-resolve the interpreter first:
744: 
745: ```bash
746: if [ ! -f graphify-out/.graphify_python ]; then
747:     GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)
748:     if [ -n "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" ]; then
749:         PYTHON=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
750:         case "$PYTHON" in *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) PYTHON="python3" ;; esac
751:     else
752:         PYTHON="python3"
753:     fi
754:     mkdir -p graphify-out
755:     "$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)"
756: fi
757: ```
758: 
759: ## For --update and --cluster-only
760: 
761: Both are non-default subcommands. `--update` re-extracts only new or changed files; `--cluster-only` reruns clustering on the existing graph. See `references/update.md` for both flows.
762: 
763: ---
764: 
765: ## For /graphify query
766: 
767: When `graphify-out/graph.json` already exists and the user asks a question about the corpus, answer from the graph rather than rebuilding it:
768: 
769: ```bash
770: graphify query "<question>"
771: ```
772: 
773: Before traversal, expand the question against the graph's own vocabulary so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise. If the `graphify query` CLI is unavailable, fall back to an inline NetworkX traversal of `graphify-out/graph.json`. Answer using only what the graph output contains, and quote `source_location` when citing a specific fact. For that vocab-expansion step, the BFS/DFS traversal modes, the `--budget` cap, the NetworkX fallback, `save-result` feedback, and the `/graphify path` and `/graphify explain` flows, see `references/query.md`.
774: 
775: ---
776: 
777: ## For /graphify add and --watch
778: 
779: Neither is part of the default build. When the user runs `/graphify add <url>` to fetch a URL into the corpus, or passes `--watch` to auto-rebuild on file changes, see `references/add-watch.md`.
780: 
781: ---
782: 
783: ## For the commit hook and native AGENTS.md integration
784: 
785: When the user asks to install the post-commit auto-rebuild hook or wire graphify into a project's AGENTS.md, see `references/hooks.md`.
786: 
787: ---
788: 
789: ## Honesty Rules
790: 
791: - Never invent an edge. If unsure, use AMBIGUOUS.
792: - Never skip the corpus check warning.
793: - Always show token cost in the report.
794: - Never hide cohesion scores behind symbols - show the raw number.
795: - Never run HTML viz on a graph with more than 5,000 nodes without warning the user.

args.CommandLine:
mkdir -p graphify-out
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import sys, json
from graphify.build import build_from_json
from graphify.cluster import cluster, score_all
from graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions
from graphify.report import generate
from graphify.export import to_json
from pathlib import Path

extraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
detection  = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

G = build_from_json(extraction, root='.', directed=False)
if G.number_of_nodes() == 0:
    print('ERROR: Graph is empty - extraction produced no nodes.')
    raise SystemExit(1)
communities = cluster(G)
cohesion = score_all(G, communities)
tokens = {'input': extraction.get('input_tokens', 0), 'output': extraction.get('output_tokens', 0)}
gods = god_nodes(G)
surprises = surprising_connections(G, communities)
labels = {cid: 'Community ' + str(cid) for cid in communities}
questions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)

wrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json', force=False)
if not wrote:
    print('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json')
    raise SystemExit(1)
report = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, gods, surprises, detection, tokens, '.', suggested_questions=questions)
Path('graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding='utf-8')
analysis = {
    'communities': {str(k): v for k, v in communities.items()},
    'cohesion': {str(k): v for k, v in cohesion.items()},
    'gods': gods,
    'surprises': surprises,
    'questions': questions,
}
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json').write_text(json.dumps(analysis, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
print(f'Graph: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, {len(communities)} communities')
"
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import json
from pathlib import Path
from graphify.diagnostics import diagnose_extraction, format_diagnostic_report

extraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
summary = diagnose_extraction(extraction, directed=False, root='.')
print(format_diagnostic_report(summary))
flags = [f'{summary[k]} {label}' for k, label in (
    ('dangling_endpoint_edges', 'dangling-endpoint edges'),
    ('missing_endpoint_edges', 'missing-endpoint edges'),
    ('self_loop_edges', 'self-loop edges'),
    ('directed_same_endpoint_collapsed_edges', 'collapsed (directed) edges'),
    ('undirected_same_endpoint_collapsed_edges', 'collapsed (undirected) edges'),
) if summary.get(k, 0)]
print('GRAPH HEALTH WARNING: ' + '; '.join(flags) + ' - graph may be incomplete/corrupt.' if flags else 'Graph health: OK (no dangling/missing/collapsed edges).')
"
args.toolSummary: Build graph, cluster, analyze, and check health

import sys, json
from graphify.build import build_from_json
from graphify.cluster import score_all
from graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions
from graphify.report import generate
from graphify.export import to_json
from pathlib import Path

extraction = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
detection  = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
analysis   = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_analysis.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

G = build_from_json(extraction, root='.', directed=False)
communities = {int(k): v for k, v in analysis['communities'].items()}
cohesion = {int(k): v for k, v in analysis['cohesion'].items()}
tokens = {'input': extraction.get('input_tokens', 0), 'output': extraction.get('output_tokens', 0)}

labels = {
    0: 'Dataset Ingestion & ENTSO-E/Fingrid Fetcher',
    1: 'Entire.io Agent Session Hooks',
    2: 'Level 2 Situational Dashboard & Data Loader',
    3: 'Official Scoring Engine & Metric Tests',
    4: 'Submission Schema Validator',
    5: 'Evaluation Pipeline & Privacy Guards',
    6: 'Causal Feature Store & Rolling Stats',
    7: 'Walk-Forward LightGBM Training Suite',
    8: 'Conformal Calibration & Prediction Constraints',
    9: 'End-to-End Pipeline & Schema Tests',
    10: 'Anti-Leakage Availability Verification',
    11: 'Forecast Origin Template Generator',
    12: 'SHAP TreeExplainer Attribution',
    13: 'Nord Pool Data Licensing Rules',
    14: 'CI Verification Runner Script',
    15: 'Source Package Root',
    16: 'Test Suite Package Root',
}

questions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)

report = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, analysis['gods'], analysis['surprises'], detection, tokens, '.', suggested_questions=questions)
Path('graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding='utf-8')
Path('graphify-out/.graphify_labels.json').write_text(json.dumps({str(k): v for k, v in labels.items()}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')
wrote = to_json(G, communities, 'graphify-out/graph.json', community_labels=labels)
if not wrote:
    print('ERROR: refused to shrink graphify-out/graph.json')
print('Report updated with community labels')
"

import json
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from graphify.detect import save_manifest
from graphify.cli import _stamped_manifest_files

detect = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_detect.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
extract = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/.graphify_extract.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

_corpus = detect.get('all_files') or detect['files']
_pf = Path('graphify-out/.graphify_partial.txt')
_partial = {l.strip() for l in _pf.read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines() if l.strip()} if _pf.exists() else set()
_manifest_files = _stamped_manifest_files(_corpus, extract, Path('.'), partial_source_files=_partial)
_sem_types = ('document', 'paper', 'image')
_dispatched = {f for t, fl in detect['files'].items() if t in _sem_types for f in fl}
_stamped = {f for fl in _manifest_files.values() for f in fl}
_cleared = _dispatched - _stamped
_scan = {f for fl in _corpus.values() for f in fl}
save_manifest(_manifest_files, root='.', scan_corpus=_scan, clear_semantic=_cleared or None)

input_tok = extract.get('input_tokens', 0)
output_tok = extract.get('output_tokens', 0)

cost_path = Path('graphify-out/cost.json')
if cost_path.exists():
    cost = json.loads(cost_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
else:
    cost = {'runs': [], 'total_input_tokens': 0, 'total_output_tokens': 0}

cost['runs'].append({
    'date': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
    'input_tokens': input_tok,
    'output_tokens': output_tok,
    'files': detect.get('total_files', 0),
})
cost['total_input_tokens'] += input_tok
cost['total_output_tokens'] += output_tok
cost_path.write_text(json.dumps(cost, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding='utf-8')

print(f'This run: {input_tok:,} input tokens, {output_tok:,} output tokens')
print(f'All time: {cost[\"total_input_tokens\"]:,} input, {cost[\"total_output_tokens\"]:,} output ({len(cost[\"runs\"])} runs)')
"

### Teil 1: aFRR- & mFRR-Daten von *vor* Juni 2026 (`< 2026-06-01`)

#### Was die Organisatoren sagen:
1. **Erlaubt:** Ihr dürft historische aFRR- und mFRR-Preis- und Volumendaten von Fingrid aus der Zeit **vor Juni 2026** (z. B. Jan–Mai 2026 oder 2025) herunterladen.
2. **Der Haken (Methodik-Wechsel im Mai/Juni 2026):** Nordisch/Finnisch wurde die Berechnung des **Imbalance Price (`fi_imbalance_price`, Dataset 319)** auf einen **volumenbasierten Ansatz (Volume-based / dual-to-single / mFRR-dominance Kopplung)** umgestellt.
   - Das heißt: Vor Juni 2026 galt eine andere mathematische Formel, wie aus `mFRR Up/Down` und `aFRR` der finale `imbalance_price` berechnet wurde.
   - Wenn man das LightGBM-Modell für `p50` (`imbalance_price`) direkt auf Daten von vor Juni 2026 trainiert, lernt das Modell eine **veraltete Preisformel** und verschlechtert sich auf dem Oktober-Testzeitraum!

#### Wie wir das clever nutzen (ohne uns die Preisformel zu vergiften):
1. **7-Tage-Lags (`168h`) für den Start der Trainingsperiode auffüllen:**
   Aktuell startet `inputs.parquet` am `2026-05-31 21:00 UTC`. Für die ersten Tage im Juni fehlen daher die 7-Tage-Lags (`imb_spread_lag_168h`, `mfrr_dir_lag_168h`). Wenn wir den Mai 2026 als **Lag-Buffer** hinzuladen, haben alle Juni-Trainingszeilen sofort vollständige Lags.
2. **Pre-June Daten NUR für das Richtungs- (`mFRR direction`) & Volatilitäts-Regime nutzen (oder mit Regime-Feature `is_new_methodology = 1`):**
   - Ob das Netz im Defizit (`up`) oder Überschuss (`down`) ist und wann `mFRR` aktiviert wird (Datasets `244, 106, 375, 376, 369, 347, 348`), folgt denselben physikalischen Netzgesetzen wie vor Juni.
   - Für unser **Preis-Modell (`p50`, `p10`, `p90`)** bleiben die Trainings-Targets (`target_spread`) strikt auf **ab Juni 2026** beschränkt (damit nur die neue volumenbasierte Preisformel gelernt wird!), oder wir trainieren ein Hilfsmodell auf historischen `mFRR/aFRR`-Daten, dessen Vorhersage als Feature in das Juni–Oktober-Modell einfließt.

181: def enforce_prediction_constraints(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
182:     """Enforce all mathematical submission constraints (RULE #3 & SKILL.md §3).
183: 
184:     1. Quantile monotonicity: p10 <= p50 <= p90
185:     2. Direction simplex: p_up, p_down, p_none in [0, 1] and p_up + p_down + p_none == 1.0
186:     3. Spike probability bound: p_spike_high, p_spike_low in [0, 1] and sum <= 1.0
187:     4. Data cutoff rule: data_cutoff_utc <= forecast_origin_utc
188:     """
189:     out = df.copy()
190: 
191:     # 1. Quantile monotonicity rounded to 6 decimals
192:     p50 = np.round(out["p50"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 6)
193:     p10 = np.round(np.minimum(out["p10"].to_numpy(dtype=float), p50), 6)
194:     p90 = np.round(np.maximum(out["p90"].to_numpy(dtype=float), p50), 6)
195:     out["p10"] = p10
196:     out["p50"] = p50
197:     out["p90"] = p90
198: 
199:     # 2. Direction probabilities simplex (exact sum == 1.0 after 6-decimal rounding)
200:     p_up = np.clip(out["p_up"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
201:     p_dn = np.clip(out["p_down"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
202:     p_no = np.clip(out["p_none"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
203:     dir_sum = p_up + p_dn + p_no
204:     dir_sum = np.where(dir_sum > 0.0, dir_sum, 1.0)
205:     p_up = np.round(p_up / dir_sum, 6)
206:     p_dn = np.round(p_dn / dir_sum, 6)
207:     # Adjust p_none as residual and re-clamp if rounding pushed p_up + p_dn slightly above 1.0
208:     over = (p_up + p_dn) > 1.0
209:     if np.any(over):
210:         p_dn[over] = np.round(1.0 - p_up[over], 6)
211:     p_no = np.round(np.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - p_up - p_dn), 6)
212:     out["p_up"] = p_up
213:     out["p_down"] = p_dn
214:     out["p_none"] = p_no
215: 
216:     # 3. Spike probabilities bound (p_spike_high + p_spike_low <= 1.0)
217:     s_hi = np.clip(out["p_spike_high"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
218:     s_lo = np.clip(out["p_spike_low"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
219:     s_sum = s_hi + s_lo
220:     scale = np.where(s_sum > 0.999990, 0.999990 / np.maximum(s_sum, 1e-9), 1.0)
221:     out["p_spike_high"] = np.round(s_hi * scale, 6)
222:     out["p_spike_low"] = np.round(s_lo * scale, 6)
223: 
224:     # 4. Verify data_cutoff_utc <= forecast_origin_utc
225:     orig_ts = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(out["forecast_origin_utc"], utc=True))
226:     cut_ts = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(out["data_cutoff_utc"], utc=True))
227:     if not (cut_ts <= orig_ts).all():
228:         raise AssertionError("Leakage in data_cutoff_utc: found data_cutoff_utc > forecast_origin_utc!")
229: 
230:     return out

428:     last_eval = eval_idx.max()
429: 
430:     df_eval = df_all.loc[df_all["forecast_origin_utc"].isin(eval_idx)].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
431:     pred_parts: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
432:     last_suite: ImbalanceModelSuite | None = None
433: 
434:     cur = first_eval
435:     while cur <= last_eval:
436:         nxt = cur + pd.Timedelta(days=retrain_step_days)
437:         chunk_mask = (df_eval["forecast_origin_utc"] >= cur) & (df_eval["forecast_origin_utc"] < nxt)
438:         df_chunk = df_eval.loc[chunk_mask].reset_index(drop=True)
439:         if len(df_chunk) > 0:
440:             # Strict anti-leakage filter on training rows AND target availability at `cur`
441:             tr_mask = (
442:                 (df_all["forecast_origin_utc"] <= cur)
443:                 & (df_all["target_fu_utc"] <= cur)
444:                 & df_all["target_spread"].notna()
445:             )
446:             df_tr = df_all.loc[tr_mask]
447:             suite = train_model_suite(df_tr, feature_cols, cutoff_origin_utc=cur)
448:             pred_chunk = suite.predict_frame(df_chunk, include_shap=True)
449:             pred_parts.append(pred_chunk)
450:             last_suite = suite
451:         cur = nxt
452: 
453:     if not pred_parts or last_suite is None:
454:         raise RuntimeError("No predictions generated in walk_forward_predict.")
455: 
456:     full_pred = pd.concat(pred_parts, ignore_index=True)
457:     full_pred = apply_temporal_ensembling(full_pred, min_step_for_blend=5, max_prev_weight=0.15)
458:     return full_pred, last_suite

args.Content:
"""External & Extended Data Fetcher for Turku Energia Imbalance Price Challenge.

Supports two Q&A-sanctioned extensions without modifying official build_dataset.py:
  1. Pre-June 2026 historical aFRR & mFRR price/volume/direction series from Fingrid
     (used strictly as lag buffers and physical regulation features; target imbalance_price
      training is gated to >= 2026-06-01 due to the volume-based pricing methodology switch).
  2. Fingrid 3-minute real-time open-data series (181 Wind RT, 188 Nuclear RT,
     191 Production RT, 177 Power System State/Consumption RT), resampled to 15-minute
     delivery intervals with a configurable safety lag (default: 30 minutes to match
     official Fingrid measurement series in availability.csv; configurable to 10 minutes
     if approved by the hackathon jury).

Output is written to `data/extra_inputs.parquet` in the exact 7-column schema:
  [series_id, source, dataset_id, timestamp_utc, value, unit, first_usable_origin_utc]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from src.data.loader import DEFAULT_DATA_DIR, read_long

UTC = timezone.utc
FINGRID_API_URL = "https://data.fingrid.fi/api/datasets/{dataset_id}/data"
VOLUME_PRICING_REGIME_START_UTC = pd.Timestamp("2026-05-31T21:00:00Z")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExtraFingridSeries:
    series_id: str
    dataset_id: int
    unit: str
    default_lag_minutes: int
    is_realtime_3min: bool = False
    note: str = ""


# 1. Real-time 3-minute Fingrid series highlighted in Hackathon Q&A
REALTIME_FINGRID_SERIES: list[ExtraFingridSeries] = [
    ExtraFingridSeries(
        series_id="fi_wind_rt",
        dataset_id=181,
        unit="MW",
        default_lag_minutes=30,
        is_realtime_3min=True,
        note="Wind power generation - real-time data (3-min resampled to 15-min)",
    ),
    ExtraFingridSeries(
        series_id="fi_nuclear_rt",
        dataset_id=188,
        unit="MW",
        default_lag_minutes=30,
        is_realtime_3min=True,
        note="Nuclear power generation - real-time data (3-min resampled to 15-min)",
    ),
    ExtraFingridSeries(
        series_id="fi_production_rt",
        dataset_id=191,
        unit="MW",
        default_lag_minutes=30,
        is_realtime_3min=True,
        note="Electricity production in Finland - real-time data (3-min resampled to 15-min)",
    ),
    ExtraFingridSeries(
        series_id="fi_grid_state_rt",
        dataset_id=177,
        unit="state",
        default_lag_minutes=30,
        is_realtime_3min=True,
        note="Power system state / real-time indicator (3-min resampled to 15-min)",
    ),
]

# 2. Historical pre-June 2026 aFRR & mFRR series (for 7-day lag buffer & regulation regime)
HISTORICAL_REGULATION_SERIES: list[ExtraFingridSeries] = [
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_mfrr_up_price", 244, "EUR/MWh", 60, False, "mFRR up price pre-June"),
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_mfrr_down_price", 106, "EUR/MWh", 60, False, "mFRR down price pre-June"),
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_mfrr_up_activated", 375, "MW", 60, False, "mFRR up volume pre-June"),
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_mfrr_down_activated", 376, "MW", 60, False, "mFRR down volume pre-June"),
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_mfrr_direction", 369, "-1/0/1", 60, False, "mFRR direction pre-June"),
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_afrr_up_price", 347, "EUR/MWh", 60, False, "aFRR up price pre-June"),
    ExtraFingridSeries("fi_afrr_down_price", 348, "EUR/MWh", 60, False, "aFRR down price pre-June"),
]


def compute_rt_first_usable(
    timestamp_utc: pd.Series | pd.DatetimeIndex,
    lag_minutes: int = 30,
    period_minutes: int = 15,
) -> pd.Series:
    """Compute leak-free `first_usable_origin_utc` for resampled quarter-hour measurements.

    Follows RULE #1 (`first_usable_origin_utc = delivery_start_utc + period_minutes + lag_minutes`).
    Defaults to lag_minutes=30 (matching Fingrid 124/74 in availability.csv) unless overridden
    after official jury confirmation (e.g. lag_minutes=10).
    """
    ts = pd.to_datetime(timestamp_utc, utc=True)
    total_offset = pd.Timedelta(minutes=period_minutes + int(lag_minutes))
    return pd.Series(ts + total_offset, index=getattr(timestamp_utc, "index", None))


def resample_3min_to_quarter_hour(
    raw_df: pd.DataFrame,
    spec: ExtraFingridSeries,
    rt_lag_minutes: int = 30,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Aggregate 3-minute Fingrid real-time observations into 15-minute quarter-hour buckets.

    Each 3-minute measurement inside [T, T+15min) is averaged into the quarter-hour
    starting at `T`, and `first_usable_origin_utc` is set to `T + 15min + rt_lag_minutes`.
    """
    if raw_df.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(
            columns=[
                "series_id",
                "source",
                "dataset_id",
                "timestamp_utc",
                "value",
                "unit",
                "first_usable_origin_utc",
            ]
        )

    df = raw_df.copy()
    df["start_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(df["startTime"], utc=True)
    df["value"] = pd.to_numeric(df["value"], errors="coerce")
    df = df.dropna(subset=["start_utc", "value"]).sort_values("start_utc")

    df["timestamp_utc"] = df["start_utc"].dt.floor("15min")
    grouped = df.groupby("timestamp_utc", as_index=False)["value"].mean()
    grouped["series_id"] = spec.series_id
    grouped["source"] = "fingrid_extra"
    grouped["dataset_id"] = str(spec.dataset_id)
    grouped["unit"] = spec.unit
    grouped["first_usable_origin_utc"] = compute_rt_first_usable(
        grouped["timestamp_utc"], lag_minutes=rt_lag_minutes, period_minutes=15
    )
    return grouped[
        [
            "series_id",
            "source",
            "dataset_id",
            "timestamp_utc",
            "value",
            "unit",
            "first_usable_origin_utc",
        ]
    ]


def fetch_fingrid_dataset_chunked(
    dataset_id: int,
    start_utc: datetime,
    end_utc: datetime,
    api_key: str,
    min_interval_s: float = 2.1,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Fetch a Fingrid dataset over [start_utc, end_utc] with rate limiting."""
    import requests

    session = requests.Session()
    headers = {"x-api-key": api_key, "Accept": "application/json"}
    rows: list[dict] = []
    cur = start_utc
    step = timedelta(days=14)

    while cur < end_utc:
        nxt = min(end_utc, cur + step)
        page = 1
        while True:
            params = {
                "startTime": cur.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "endTime": nxt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
                "format": "json",
                "pageSize": 20000,
                "page": page,
            }
            resp = session.get(
                FINGRID_API_URL.format(dataset_id=dataset_id),
                params=params,
                headers=headers,
                timeout=60,
            )
            time.sleep(min_interval_s)
            if resp.status_code == 404:
                break
            resp.raise_for_status()
            payload = resp.json()
            data = payload.get("data", []) if isinstance(payload, dict) else payload
            if not data:
                break
            rows.extend(data)
            pagination = payload.get("pagination", {}) if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
            last_page = pagination.get("lastPage", 1)
            if page >= last_page:
                break
            page += 1
        cur = nxt

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def load_extra_inputs(data_dir: Path | str = DEFAULT_DATA_DIR) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    """Load `data/extra_inputs.parquet` (or `.csv`) if present on disk."""
    data_dir = Path(data_dir)
    for name in ("extra_inputs.parquet", "extra_inputs.csv"):
        p = data_dir / name
        if p.exists():
            return read_long(p)
    return None


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Fetch optional extra Fingrid series (pre-June aFRR/mFRR & 181/188/191/177 RT).")
    parser.add_argument("--pre-june-start", default="2026-05-01T00:00:00Z", help="Start UTC for pre-June aFRR/mFRR lag buffer.")
    parser.add_argument("--rt-start", default="2026-05-31T21:00:00Z", help="Start UTC for 181/188/191/177 real-time series.")

   Nicht wir im Code, sondern **Fingrid / eSett (der finnische Übertragungsnetzbetreiber)** in der echten Welt!
   - **Vor Juni 2026** hat Fingrid den finnischen Ausgleichspreis (`imbalance_price`) im Wesentlichen nach dem **reinen mFRR-Preis** festgelegt.
   - **Ab Juni 2026** (genau dort, wo unser Starter-Datensatz `inputs.parquet` beginnt!) hat Fingrid seine offizielle Marktregel auf einen **volumenbasierten Ansatz (Volume-based Pricing)** umgestellt: Der `imbalance_price` wird seit Juni aus dem volumengewichteten Durchschnitt von **mFRR** und **aFRR** berechnet.

2. **Warum hat die Jury im Discord davor gewarnt?**
   Weil einige Teams im Q&A gefragt haben: *"Dürfen wir historische aFRR- und mFRR-Daten aus 2024/2025/Anfang 2026 (also vor Juni) von der Fingrid-API herunterladen, um mehr Trainingsdaten zu haben?"*
   Darauf hat die Jury geantwortet:
   - **Ja**, ihr dürft ältere aFRR/mFRR-Daten von vor Juni nutzen.
   - **Aber Vorsicht:** Vor Juni galt bei Fingrid noch die alte Preisformel! Wenn ein Team also alte Daten von vor Juni herunterlädt und sein Modell einfach blind auf den alten `imbalance_price` trainiert, lernt das Modell die **alte** Fingrid-Formel statt der **neuen** volumenbasierten Formel ab Juni.

3. **Was hat unser Modell bisher gemacht vs. was macht es jetzt?**
   - **Bisher:** Unser Datensatz (`inputs.parquet`) enthielt ohnehin nur Daten **ab Juni 2026**. Unser Modell hat also schon auf den richtigen Daten trainiert, kannte `mFRR`-Preise und `aFRR`-Preise bisher aber nur als getrennte Einzel-Features (`last_mfrr_up_price`, `last_afrr_up_price`).

     Erstens haben wir eine Schutzschranke eingebaut, falls ihr Daten von *vor* Juni dazukopiert (damit das Preis-Modell niemals auf Vor-Juni-Targets trainiert).

s_lo = m['p_spike_low'].to_numpy()

y_lo = (y < spot - 50.0).astype(float)

def pinball(y_true, y_pred, q):
    d = y_true - y_pred
    return np.mean(np.where(d >= 0, q * d, (q - 1.0) * d))

print('Current Pinball:', 0.5 * (pinball(y, p10, 0.1) + pinball(y, p90, 0.9)), 'Cov:', np.mean((y >= p10) & (y <= p90)))

- Physikalisch gilt in Finnland aber: Ein positiver Preis-Spike (`> Spot + 50 €`) kann **nur** passieren, wenn das Netz im Defizit ist (`direction == up`), und ein negativer Preis-Spike (`< Spot - 50 €`) **nur** bei Überschuss (`direction == down`)!
- Ich habe das gerade in 5 Sekunden auf den Validierungsdaten getestet: Wenn wir `p_spike_high` und `p_spike_low` leicht mit `p_up` und `p_down` koppeln (`b = 0.20`), sinkt der **Spike Brier sofort weiter von `0.0932` auf `0.0929`**!

#### Hebel B: Ein zweites Modell-Verfahren im Ensemble (z. B. CatBoost / Ridge / Multi-Seed LightGBM Blend)
- Aktuell wird `p50` von **einem einzigen LightGBM-Baum-Ensemble (`RANDOM_SEED = 42`)** vorhergesagt.
- Im Machine Learning (und bei Kaggle/Energie-Hackathons) bringt das **Mitteln von 2–3 leicht unterschiedlichen Bäumen** (z. B. ein flacherer, stark regularisierter Baum `num_leaves=15` + unser Standard-Baum `num_leaves=23`, oder L1 + Huber-Loss) fast immer noch einmal **`-0.15 €` bis `-0.30 €/MWh`** beim MAE und glättet Ausreißer, ohne dass man neue Daten braucht!

---

### Mein ehrliches Fazit:
- **Bei den Daten:** Mit den offiziellen Daten + deinen **105.307 Fingrid-Extra-Zeilen** (`181` Echtzeit-Wind, `188` Kernkraft, `191` Produktion, `177` Netzstatus + April/Mai `aFRR/mFRR`-Historie) haben wir datenseitig alles Relevante ausgeschöpft, ohne ein Regel-Risiko (`RULE #1`) einzugehen.
- **Beim Modell:** Wenn du noch die letzten paar Zehntel-Punkte herauskitzeln willst, sind **Hebel A (Spike-Direction-Kopplung)** und **Hebel B (2-Modell-Ensemble aus flachem + tiefem LightGBM)** die einzigen beiden sauberen Hebel, die noch messbar etwas bringen.

211: def enforce_prediction_constraints(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
212:     """Enforce all mathematical submission constraints (RULE #3 & SKILL.md §3).
213: 
214:     1. Quantile monotonicity: p10 <= p50 <= p90
215:     2. Direction simplex: p_up, p_down, p_none in [0, 1] and p_up + p_down + p_none == 1.0
216:     3. Spike probability bound: p_spike_high, p_spike_low in [0, 1] and sum <= 1.0

219:     out = df.copy()

221:     # 1. Quantile monotonicity rounded to 6 decimals
222:     p50 = np.round(out["p50"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 6)
223:     p10 = np.round(np.minimum(out["p10"].to_numpy(dtype=float), p50), 6)
224:     p90 = np.round(np.maximum(out["p90"].to_numpy(dtype=float), p50), 6)
225:     out["p10"] = p10
226:     out["p50"] = p50
227:     out["p90"] = p90

229:     # 2. Direction probabilities simplex (exact sum == 1.0 after 6-decimal rounding)

231:     p_dn = np.clip(out["p_down"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
232:     p_no = np.clip(out["p_none"].to_numpy(dtype=float), 0.0, 1.0)
233:     dir_sum = p_up + p_dn + p_no
234:     dir_sum = np.where(dir_sum > 0.0, dir_sum, 1.0)
235:     p_up = np.round(p_up / dir_sum, 6)
236:     p_dn = np.round(p_dn / dir_sum, 6)
237:     # Adjust p_none as residual and re-clamp if rounding pushed p_up + p_dn slightly above 1.0
238:     over = (p_up + p_dn) > 1.0
239:     if np.any(over):
240:         p_dn[over] = np.round(1.0 - p_up[over], 6)
241:     p_no = np.round(np.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - p_up - p_dn), 6)
242:     out["p_up"] = p_up
243:     out["p_down"] = p_dn
244:     out["p_none"] = p_no

1: # Evaluation Report — Turku Energia Imbalance Price Forecasting Challenge
2: **Event:** Since AI Hackathon 2026 (6–8 Nov 2026, Turku)

7: ## 1. Executive Summary
8: 
9: To support operational decision-making for Turku Energia's production shift supervisors and electricity traders, we built an end-to-end probabilistic forecasting and situational awareness system covering the 10-hour (40 quarter-hour) horizon at hourly origins:
10: 
11: 1. **Spread-Decomposition Forecasting**: Under Finnish market rules (effective 1 June 2026), the imbalance price equals the day-ahead spot price when there is no dominant mFRR direction (`fi_mfrr_direction == 0`) and deviates upward/downward as a volume-weighted function of activated mFRR and fulfilled aFRR demand. Because the Nord Pool spot price (`fi_spot_price`) is published at 14:00 Finnish time on D-1 (`first_usable_origin_utc <= t`), we decompose the target into:
12:    $$P_{\text{imbalance}}(t + k) = P_{\text{spot}}(t + k) + \Delta P(t + k)$$
13:    where $\Delta P = P_{\text{imbalance}} - P_{\text{spot}}$ is the **imbalance spread**.
14: 2. **Strict Anti-Leakage Architecture (`first_usable_origin_utc <= t`)**: Every feature lookup, rolling window, and walk-forward training label is masked by `first_usable_origin_utc <= forecast_origin_utc` (`../src/data/loader.py`, `src/features/build_features.py`, `src/models/train.py`).
15: 3. **Validation Period Results (`7 Sep – 4 Oct 2026`, 672 origins / 26,700 scored rows)**:
16:    - **MAE (`p50`)**: **43.35 EUR/MWh** vs. Baseline **66.20 EUR/MWh** (**-34.5%** error reduction, `-22.86 EUR/MWh`).
17:    - **Uncertainty Calibration (`p10`/`p90` Mean Pinball Loss)**: **12.43** vs. Baseline **24.18** (**-48.6%** reduction) with **80.00% empirical P10–P90 coverage** (exact 80% target vs. Baseline 68.29%).
18:    - **Exceptional Price Identification (`±50 EUR/MWh` Mean Brier)**: **0.0943** vs. Baseline **0.1132** (**-16.7%** improvement).
19:    - **Balancing Direction (`up`/`down`/`none` 3-Class Brier)**: **0.4132** vs. Baseline **0.4509** (**-8.4%** improvement).

47: 1. **Short Horizon (`Steps 1–8`, Hours 1–2 — Real-Time Grid Inertia)**:
48:    - Weather front timing errors, industrial load deviations, and thermal unit outages persist over 1–3 hours.
49:    - At origin $t$, the latest usable realized consumption (`fi_consumption`, 30-min publication delay) compared against the day-ahead consumption forecast (`fi_consumption_fc_da`) immediately reveals the **real-time consumption forecast error** (`cons_forecast_error_30m`).
50:    - Similarly, the latest usable realized imbalance spread (`last_imbalance_spread`, 60-min delay), mFRR net regulation volume (`last_mfrr_net_activated`), and aFRR price spreads (`last_afrr_up_spread`, `last_afrr_down_spread`) measure active balancing stress right before origin $t$.
51: 2. **Medium-to-Long Horizon (`Steps 9–40`, Hours 3–10 — Forward Structural Drivers)**:
52:    - Beyond 2 hours, persistence decays and the forecast is governed by **already published day-ahead plans** for the target delivery quarter-hour (`delivery_start_utc`):
53:      - **Spot Price Anchor & Ramps (`spot_at_delivery`, `spot_ramp_1h`, `spot_ramp_3h`)**: Steep upward spot price ramps during morning/evening peaks indicate tight day-ahead reserve margins where small forecast errors trigger large upward mFRR price spikes.
54:      - **Residual Load & Wind Ramps (`residual_load_da_at_delivery`, `wind_da_ramp_3h`, `wind_share_da_at_delivery`)**: High wind penetration or steep 3-hour wind ramps amplify balancing volume errors, widening the P10–P90 interval and increasing `p_spike_high` / `p_spike_low`.
55:      - **Cross-Border Coupling (`fi_se3_flow_30m`, `fi_no4_flow_30m`, `fi_se1_flow_30m`, `fi_ee_capacity_da`, `se1/se3/ee_imb_spread_120m`)**: High net imports or constrained Estlink (`FI–EE`) transfer capacity limit Finland's ability to absorb domestic forecast errors via neighboring bidding zones.

59: ## 3. Data Availability & Anti-Leakage Architecture (Rule #1)
60: 
61: Every data access in the repository enforces `first_usable_origin_utc <= forecast_origin_utc`:
62: 
63: 1. **`FeatureStore` Dual-Matrix Masking (`../src/features/build_features.py`)**:
64:    - Pivots `inputs.parquet` and `spot_nordpool.csv` into two aligned wide matrices indexed by `timestamp_utc`: `val_wide` (values) and `fu_wide` (`first_usable_origin_utc`).
65:    - `FeatureStore.lookup_at(series_id, target_timestamps, origin_timestamps)` explicitly masks every element with `valid_mask = (~fus.isna()) & (fus <= orig_idx)`, returning `NaN` for any value not yet published at $t$.
66:    - `FeatureStore.latest_usable_timestamp_per_origin(series_id, origins)` uses binary search (`searchsorted`) on `first_usable_origin_utc` and asserts `(used_fu <= origins).all()`, guaranteeing that lagged features reflect the exact publication lag of each source (30 min for measured load/flows, 60 min for imbalance/mFRR/aFRR, 120 min for ENTSO-E neighboring imbalance).
67: 2. **Causal Walk-Forward Training (`../src/models/train.py`)**:
68:    - During walk-forward training at chunk boundary `cur`, a historical training row `(origin, step)` is included **if and only if** both `forecast_origin_utc <= cur` **and** `target_fu_utc <= cur` (where `target_fu_utc` is the `first_usable_origin_utc` of `fi_imbalance_price` at `delivery_start_utc`).
69:    - No future target label that is still unpublished at `cur` ever enters the training set.
70: 3. **Automated Anti-Leakage Test Suite (`../tests/test_data_leakage.py`)**:
71:    - Verifies that mutating future rows (`first_usable_origin_utc > t`) by $+10^6$ produces **zero numerical change** in features or predictions at origin $t$.
